name: Critical minerals
summary: China extended its pause on some rare-earth export controls to 10 Jan 2027 on 9 Nov; April 2025 licensing stays
state: On 9 Nov China's commerce ministry extended its suspension of some rare-earth export controls, due to end on 10 Nov, to 10 Jan 2027; the pause covers five rare earths, processing technology and some battery and graphite items (S&P Global). Controls imposed in April 2025 on seven heavy rare earths, including dysprosium and terbium, remain in force. Searches on 18 Nov found no production stoppages outside China linked to export bans, so Watch holds.
for_you: Makers of electric vehicles, wind turbines, electronics and defence equipment outside China are most exposed to rare-earth licensing delays, which tend to show up first as longer lead times and higher component costs.
rubric_hit: Watch: Chinese licensing on seven heavy rare earths still in force; no reported production stoppages outside China (Alert line)

sources.title: S&P Global — China extends rare earth export suspension to January 2027

why: Rare earths, gallium, germanium and graphite are chokepoints for chips, EVs and defence — and China dominates processing.
drivers: Export controls, trade disputes, mine outages, stockpiling.

rubric.alert: Export bans in force that are causing reported production stoppages outside China.
rubric.watch: New export controls announced or licensing slowed.
rubric.normal: No new export restrictions in the past month.
